message.content:
Paris has many iconic landmarks, but if you’re looking for **the single “most famous” spot**, it’s almost always the **Eiffel Tower** (La Tour eifflé).  

*Why it tops the list:*  
- It was built as a temporary structure for the 1889 Exposition Universelle and instantly became a symbol of French ingenuity.  
- Every year millions of visitors climb its iron lattice—over 7 million people have taken the elevator up since 2000 alone!  
- Its silhouette is recognized worldwide; it appears in countless films, postcards, and logos.  
- From its observation decks you get sweeping views over the Seine, Montmartre, and even the Arc de Triomphe—a perfect photo‑op.

Other contenders often mentioned include:

| Landmark | Why it matters |
|----------|----------------|
| **Louvre Museum** | Home to thousands of masterpieces including the Mona Lisa. |
| **Notre‑Dame Cathedral** | Gothic architecture icon (though damaged by fire in 2019). |
| **Arc de Triomphe & Champs‑Élysées** | Symbolic monument celebrating France’s military victories. |

But when someone says “I’m going to Paris,” they usually mean seeing the Eiffel Tower first—and then perhaps strolling along the Seine or visiting one of those other world‑class sites.
